shorts.title: What you will learn: Binary tree
shorts.hook: Print numbers in sorted order with no sort call.
shorts.script: Print numbers in sorted order with no sort call. Today we build a tree. Each node has two children. Small numbers go left, and big numbers go right. A binary search tree keeps its keys in order. For each node, every key in the left side is smaller, and every key in the right side is bigger. Recursion fits trees well. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Binary tree.

shorts.title: Binary tree in one minute
shorts.hook: A binary search tree keeps its keys in order.
shorts.script: A binary search tree keeps its keys in order. For each node, every key in the left side is smaller, and every key in the right side is bigger. Recursion fits trees well. To insert, compare the key, then go left or right, and repeat. Insert returns the root of the tree after the change. An empty spot is the base case. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Binary tree in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Contains follows one path only. An empty spot means the key is not in the tree. A match means the key is in the tree. Otherwise it goes left or right, as insert did. Four is in the tree, so we get true. Seven is not, so we get false. Height is one plus the height of the taller child. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Printing before the left side
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The keys come out as five three one four, which is not sorted. The code prints the node before the left side. Visit left first, then print, then visit right. The order of the three lines decides the traversal. Left, node, right gives sorted order. Node first gives preorder, which is not sorted. A binary search tree keeps keys in order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: PRINTING BEFORE THE LEFT SIDE
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Printing before the left side.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Why did the tree win the race? It had strong roots, and it never lost its balance.
shorts.script: Why did the tree win the race? It had strong roots, and it never lost its balance. Write a function that returns the smallest key in a binary search tree. Hint: keep going left. Write your answer in the comments. A binary search tree keeps keys in order. Smaller keys go left, and bigger keys go right. Inorder traversal prints the keys in sorted order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
